# The allocation-count matrix — blocks the self-host allocates PER ROUND for
# each cell (self_host_alloc_count_matrix_test.go, #7351).
#
# Format: <cell> <blocks> <note>
#
# The leak matrix classifies each cell clean-or-leak, which is layout-free and
# therefore blind to a program allocating more blocks than its values need —
# the whole of #7351 was invisible to it. A number falling is progress and
# belongs to the change that earns it; a number RISING is a volume regression
# no runtime detector reports. Regenerate with FERN_ALLOC_COUNT_DUMP=1 — never
# hand-edit a number without a measured run.
scalar_only           0   none: the struct, read only by its fields, is split into them
bare_arr              1   array buffer only
arr_field             1   array buffer only: the struct is split into its fields
bare_str_sso          1   one string block: there is no inline small-string form (#7351)
str_field_sso         1   one string block, for the same reason; the struct is split into its fields
bare_str_heap         1   one block per heap string
str_field_heap        1   one string block: the struct is split into its fields
capture_free_fn_value 0   none: the capture-free function value is a static cell (#9839) and the struct is split
arr_and_str_heap      2   array buffer + one string block: the struct is split into its fields
str_self_append_chain 6   eight `+` per round: the accumulator grows in place (__fern_str_grow, #10960), else a fresh __fern_str_concat box
